title: Archive targets in public circulation: reverse bridges through the British Newspaper Archive corpus
method: New source-registry actors were searched against the canonical BNA master. Only records that add a public event, transaction, exhibition, gift, prize, or circulation state were retained. Newspaper OCR is treated as a routing layer and should be image-checked before verbatim quotation in publication.

events.event: Belfast Naturalists' Field Club award notice gives prize No. 14 to Charles Elcock for a set of twenty-five microscopic slides.
events.significance: A bounded 25-slide set is publicly recognized before the 1885 Type Slide advertisements and in the same Belfast milieu from which Elcock's professional trade developed.

events.event: Independent newspaper repetition of the Field Club prize for Elcock's set of twenty-five microscopic slides.
events.significance: Corroborates the award wording and date; use as duplicate confirmation rather than a second event.

events.event: A report groups Elcock's microscopic preparations with other Belfast natural-history work as examples of thorough scientific work.
events.significance: Shows local public/scientific reputation of the preparations in the year Whipple's later account identifies as the period in which his slides began to be sold through agents.

bridges.new_chain: local prize set (25 slides) → public scientific reputation → postal-society object/note circulation → standardized Type Slides → priced multi-city retail → surviving labelled Type Slide drawers

bridges.archive_target: St Andrews Norman-labelled slides + Norman 1872 catalogue

events.event: A repeated item titled 'Microscopic Varieties' describes Mr. Norman showing a large series of microscopic slides containing minute sections and preparations across a very wide range of animal and vegetable objects.
events.significance: Public exhibition/display precedes Norman's 1872 classified catalogue. The commercial preparer's range was already being presented as a comprehensive series of microscopic objects rather than isolated curiosities.

related_corpus: R44412 (1872 Science-Gossip exchange: 'Norman's prepared microscopical slides and others')
R47680 (1875 Monthly Microscopical Journal: Norman-mounted diatoms used to test an objective)
bridges.new_chain: public range/display → classified commercial catalogue → secondary exchange → optical test use → surviving institutional slides

bridges.archive_target: Whipple mixed cabinet with Pritchard catalogue-derived labels

events.event: Reports thank Andrew Pritchard for presents of microscopic slides together with books and plates to a northern microscopical/natural-history context.
events.significance: Pritchard's material and print objects circulated together as gifts long after his early commercial catalogue work. This is a useful public counterpart to the Whipple cabinet where catalogue-derived labels remain attached to slides.

related_corpus: R43685 (1876 Science-Gossip retrospective cites Pritchard's 1837 catalogue and mounted-object prices)
bridges.new_chain: early catalogue/price system → labelled commercial slides → gifts of slides + books + plates → later mixed cabinet survival

method_result: The newspaper corpus is most useful after a named surviving archive is known. Instead of broad searches for 'microscope slides', the archive supplies an actor/product identity and BNA returns dated public states—prize, display, gift, sale, auction or reputation—that can be inserted between workshop/catalogue evidence and current custody.
guard: Repeated newspaper notices may be syndicated or copied versions of one event. They corroborate wording/geography but are not counted as separate circulation events without independent event evidence.
